title: Snapshot's regular-file check can be raced into archiving an outside-scope symlink target
summary: KCS observes a direct child's file type before performing a separate pathname-based `fs::read`. A lower-trust local writer that can rename a checked direct child can replace it with a symlink to a victim-readable file outside the scope before the read, causing snapshot to archive those outside bytes under the benign in-scope name.

affectedLocations.label: entrypoint
affectedLocations.detail: Manual snapshot opens the current repository, computes filename exclusions, and calls `snapshot_filtered`.

affectedLocations.label: root_control
affectedLocations.detail: `DirEntry::file_type` is observed before a separate pathname-based `fs::read` with no descriptor or inode binding.

affectedLocations.label: archive_sink
affectedLocations.detail: Bytes read through the replacement path are hashed, optionally written to raw CAS, and bound under the benign filename.

affectedLocations.label: cas_sink
affectedLocations.detail: `ObjectStore::write_raw` persists the supplied buffer under its content hash.

affectedLocations.label: closest_control
affectedLocations.detail: Snapshot holds only the `.kcs` store lock; it does not exclude external working-directory renames.

codeEvidence.label: Manual snapshot reaches the filtered snapshot path
codeEvidence.explanation: The ordinary `kcs snapshot` path reaches the repository snapshot builder after only name-based exclusions. A lower-trust writer races the selected working root while this victim command runs.

codeEvidence.label: Stable non-regular entries are skipped before the read
codeEvidence.explanation: `entry.file_type()` protects only the filesystem state observed at this point. A stable symlink is skipped, but the accepted `path` remains a mutable pathname that can be renamed before use.

codeEvidence.label: The accepted name is reopened by pathname
codeEvidence.explanation: The later `fs::read(&path)` performs a fresh pathname resolution. If the direct-child name was replaced with an outside symlink after the type observation, these lines read and bind the target bytes under the earlier benign filename.

codeEvidence.label: Snapshot persists the followed bytes
codeEvidence.explanation: `write_raw` stores exactly the buffer returned by the racy pathname read, so the outside target's bytes become raw CAS state when snapshot calls the builder with `store_raw=true`.

codeEvidence.label: The snapshot lock does not cover working-directory renames
codeEvidence.explanation: The held lock serializes `.kcs` updates by cooperating KCS processes. It does not stop an external lower-trust writer from renaming a direct child in the working root during the check/read gap.

rootCause.summary: The violated invariant is that the filesystem object accepted as a regular direct child must be the same object whose bytes are hashed and archived. `build_working_tree_with_normalize()` observes `DirEntry::file_type()` and later calls `fs::read(&path)` on a mutable pathname, with no descriptor-bound no-follow open, inode comparison, post-open type check, or working-directory writer exclusion.

validation.method: static source trace plus local/offline deterministic interleaving PoC
validation.summary: The source trace confirms separate file-type and read operations on the same mutable pathname. The included PoC creates a synthetic scope, observes a direct child as regular, swaps it to a symlink to `../outside-victim.txt`, and shows a path reopen following and hashing the outside bytes.
assertions: A stable symlink is skipped only if it is already present when `entry.file_type()` runs.
`fs::read(&path)` is a later pathname open and can follow a symlink installed after the type observation.
Snapshot passes `store_raw=true`, causing the followed bytes to be persisted through `ObjectStore::write_raw` and named in the tree.
limitations: No live KCS timing stress harness measured race win probability.
No standalone lower-trust read path from owner-only raw CAS was proven.
The PoC is a deterministic model of the interleaving rather than an end-to-end CLI race.

attackPath.summary: A local lower-trust writer presents a regular direct-child file in a scope the operator snapshots, then atomically replaces that name with a symlink to a victim-readable outside file after KCS observes the type and before the later read. Snapshot follows the replacement and records the outside bytes under the benign direct-child name.

dataflow.summary: direct-child name -> `DirEntry::file_type()` acceptance -> attacker rename to outside symlink -> `fs::read(&path)` -> `ObjectStore::write_raw()` -> tree entry under benign name
dataflow.source: lower-trust local writer controls one direct-child pathname and symlink target
dataflow.sink: raw CAS object and snapshot tree entry
dataflow.outcome: outside-scope bytes enter authoritative archive state under an in-scope filename

reachability.summary: The path requires concurrent rename authority in the selected root, victim read permission on the outside target, an operator status or snapshot invocation, and a successful timing interleaving.
reachability.attacker: lower-trust local content contributor or process with write authority in the selected scope
reachability.entrypoint: ordinary `kcs snapshot`; `kcs status` reaches the same read path without raw persistence
reachability.outcome: snapshot archive integrity and scope-boundary confusion

impact.why: The primitive can place victim-readable outside bytes into the selected scope's authoritative snapshot and raw CAS.

likelihood.why: The source permits the interleaving, but exploitation needs local directory-write authority and a race win; losing interleavings usually skip the entry, archive benign bytes, or return an I/O error.

limitations: Stable symlinks present during the initial file-type observation are skipped.
The owner-only `.kcs` parent normally limits later disclosure to the lower-trust writer.
No race reliability measurement was retained.

remediation.summary: Bind the type decision and byte read to one opened filesystem object. Open each direct child relative to an opened scope directory with no-follow semantics, validate the opened descriptor as a regular file, and read/hash/store from that descriptor rather than reopening a mutable pathname.
remediation.minimalFix: Replace the pre-read `DirEntry::file_type()` plus later `fs::read(&path)` sequence with a descriptor-bound no-follow open, `fstat` regular-file check, and descriptor read. On platforms without that primitive, fail closed or use a capability-filesystem abstraction.
regressionTests: A stable symlink direct child remains skipped with a warning.
A test hook that replaces a checked regular child with an outside symlink before the read must not hash or archive the outside marker.
`status` and `snapshot` variants should both exercise the shared builder.
A concurrent rename-loop stress test should never produce a tree or status hash for the outside target bytes.
